{"content": "1|// ★ THE DENOMINATOR, EXTRACTED SO IT CAN BE RUN INSTEAD OF GREPPED.
2|//
3|// `lspVerifiedPct` was computed inline in health.js, so the only way to guard it was to
4|// assert regexes over that file — eight of them, all spelling. the field test rates this
5|// denominator among the fields they ACTUALLY USED (they checked the 833/1599 arithmetic
6|// against it), which makes a test that cannot fail on a wrong number the worst kind to
7|// have here.
8|//
9|// Pulling it out is a small refactor with a large consequence: the invariant becomes
10|// checkable by calling it with rows and comparing integers.
11|//
12|// THE INVARIANTS, each of which was a real defect at some point:
13|//
14|//  1. DIVIDE BY THE VERIFIABLE SUBSET, NOT BY EVERY CALLS EDGE. Dividing by all calls
15|//     reported 12% on a repo where every verifiable edge was verified — a number that
16|//     read as a coverage failure and was an accounting one.
17|//  2. OUT-OF-SCOPE EDGES NEVER ENTER, AND NEVER MIGRATE IN. An edge outside the tracked
18|//     corpus is not verifiable debt; if a backend for its language later lands, it must
19|//     not silently appear in the denominator and drop the percentage.
20|//  3. UNVERIFIABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION IS NOT UNVERIFIED-BY-OMISSION. A JS edge in a C++-only
21|//     collection was never going to be verified. Counting it as a miss blames the tool
22|//     for a language it does not claim.
23|//  4. UNKNOWN SCOPE ≠ EVERYTHING IN SCOPE. If the tracked-file list cannot be read, the
24|//     honest answer is that scope is unknown — not that every edge is in it.
25|
26|// Languages an LSP backend in this server can actually verify. Anything else is
27|// unverifiable by construction.
28|export const LSP_VERIFIABLE_LANGUAGES = new Set(['cpp', 'c', 'cxx', 'cc', 'h', 'hpp']);
29|
30|/**
31| * @param {Array<{lang: string, c: number, inScope?: boolean}>} langScopeRows
32| *        one row per (language, scope) bucket with a count.
33| * @param {number} verified  edges actually verified by an LSP backend.
34| * @returns {{
35| *   verifiable: number, verified: number, pct: number,
36| *   denominator: string,
37| *   outOfScope: number,
38| *   unverifiable: Array<{reason: string, lang: string, count: number}>
39| * }}
40| */
41|export function computeCoverage(langScopeRows = [], verified = 0) {
42|  const outOfScopeRows = langScopeRows.filter((r) => r.inScope === false);
43|  const inScopeRows = langScopeRows.filter((r) => r.inScope !== false);
44|
45|  const verifiable = inScopeRows
46|    .filter((r) => LSP_VERIFIABLE_LANGUAGES.has(r.lang))
47|    .reduce((a, r) => a + r.c, 0);
48|

content:
Fixed the population mismatch.

Cause: health.js divided all LSP_VERIFIED edges—including non-CALLS relations, unsupported languages, and out-of-scope files—by only verifiable, in-scope CALLS.

Changes:
  - mcp/stdio/query/verbs/health.js:1497 now collects verified counts alongside CALLS counts, using the same caller-file scope.
  - mcp/stdio/query/coverage-denominator.js:40 filters numerator and denominator identically.
  - Preserved lspVerifiedEdges as the global count and added lspVerifiedVerifiableInScopeCalls to expose the actual numerator. Both percentage fields use the corrected ratio; no clamping.

Tests cover mixed relations/languages, out-of-scope files, aggregation across files, zero/partial/full verification, and unknown scope. The regression fixture has 949 verified edges and 19 eligible calls; with 10 eligible verified calls it correctly reports 53%.

Verification: 24 focused tests passed; existing collection-coverage and code-intel tests also passed. The broader query-suite run timed out, so I can’t claim a full-suite pass.
